name_es: Hermann de Dalmacia (traductor latino de la Chronica mendosa)
role_place: Translator at Toledo for the Toledan (Cluniac) Corpus, c. 1142-43; the Bibliander 1543 table of contents names him for the Chronica mendosa.
why_relevant: His Latin of the Chronica mendosa names Aisha as Ayſca, daughter of Eubokara (Abu Bakr) and wife of the prophet, in a political narrative.
fame: Known mainly as a translator for Peter the Venerable's Toledan corpus; not a major author. Attribution of the Chronica mendosa text to him rests on the 1543 table of contents, not on a modern study I checked.

role_place: Humanist at Bruges and Oxford; his De veritate fidei christianae (printed 1543, Basel) contains the Mahomet censure reprinted in Bibliander 1543.
why_relevant: His Latin excerpt names Aisha as Aiſſa, wife of Muhammad, in a Qur'anic textual-history passage, and contains an explicit sexual passage naming Aysa (excluded).
fame: Well known humanist and educator; his Mahomet chapter is less studied than his other works.
